newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Bankar to offer venture capital firm stock.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Bankar to offer venture capital firm stock.

text.p: Hungary's Bankar group will offer the shares of a new venture capital investment company, Riziko Factory Rt (RF) for subscription from November 11 to 22, Zoltan Remenyi, Bankar's portfolio manager said on Monday.
Riziko will be Hungary's first venture capital investment firm to embrace the whole range of stock exchange and over-the-counter security transactions, including futures deals on the domestic market.
The lead manager of the subscription is Postbank Securities. @
Remenyi told a news conference Riziko also planned to be a player on the Budapest Commodity exchange and Hungary's interbank currency market.
Foreign investors have expressed interest in buying Riziko shares, Remenyi added.

Bankar said Hungary's futures and stock markets are potentially profitable but Riziko's investments will involve more risk than the Bankar's existing currency futures investment companies, Deviza Factory I and Deviza Factory II. @

"As Riziko Factory will enter the stock market, which is more volatile, we recommend to investors to place only part of their portfolio in the new company," Bankar analyst Gyorgy Szilagyi told a news conference.

Remenyi told reporters that Deviza Factory I has increased its initial capital almost fivefold since it was founded in December 1994, while the value of the shares in Deviza Factory II, which began operations in March this year, stands at 150 percent of face value. @
Bankar guarantees to buy the shares at a price it will publish regularly, and plans to list the shares of Riziko Factory and Deviza Factory II on the Budapest Stock Exchange in early 1997.
Bankar has invested more than $2.5 billion in foreign currency futures deals in Hungary in the past four years on behalf of 170 commissioners, the group said.
